# dsh-bot

**A MiniMax-Bot-style always-on agent team for DeepSeek Harness (DSH).**
Create named Bots, chat wit
h them one-on-one, pull them into groups, give them shared or private memory, schedule recurring wor
k, dispatch background tasks, and read the usage ledger — while every Bot reply is a **real DSH Agen
t session** you can open at any time.

## Why
In DSH a Session *is* an Agent. dsh-bot does not invent a second execution layer: it gives each Bot
its own real Session (grouped in a dedicated workspace), injects the Bot persona/team/memory into th
e prompt, and turns every message into one real turn. The workbench is a thin product layer on top —
so you keep native tool cards, approvals, queueing, search and model selection for free.
## Features
| Area | What you get |
| **Bot team** | Named Bots with role, instructions, avatar, model, reasoning effort, permission pre
set and pinned workspace. Chief Bot is created first and is the only one that may edit the roster an

d groups. |
| **Pinned chats** | Pin any conversation; Chief's private chat is pinned on first launc

h. |
| **Private chats** | Every message is one real Agent turn. Streaming text, tool rows, retry, c

ancel, quote, copy, markdown rendering. |
| **Group chats** | `@Name` mentions with a member picker
and `@all`, speaker routing with a per-round cap (`maxSpeakers`, default 3), group-first collaborati
on (work goes to the group, private chat stays one-to-one), auto-captured decisions in the group not
e, admin/all reply modes, `[PASS]` skipping, hop limit with a wrap-up turn, handover of the previous
conclusion, and a group note that survives clearing the chat. The main Bot can create/update/delete

groups and post into any group. |
| **Task dispatch** | `bot_dispatch_tasks` / `bot_get_tasks` / `b
ot_cancel_tasks`: batched background delegation with request-id idempotency, receipts, result relay

and cancel cascade. |
| **Background helpers** | Hidden child sessions for work that should not bloc

k the chat; the report comes back and the Bot verifies it in its own words. |
| **Memory** | Team an
d per-Bot stores, selected into the next turn under a 6,000-character budget with revision guards an

d a journal — with **automatic capture** and a review queue (see below). |
| **Schedules** | Daily /

every-N / once, delivered by the Host schedule service to a Bot session. |
| **Rich input** | Text,
images and files like the native composer: paste, drag, picker; the Bot receives absolute paths and

can read them. |
| **Avatar library** | 40 original SVG avatars; new Bots auto-match from name/role

keywords (unknown roles fall back deterministically). |
| **Usage** | Turns and characters per Bot

over 7/30/90 days; workflow-level task panel. |
| **Tool details** | Every tool call shows a one-lin
e summary (command, path, URL); expand it to read the arguments and result, with copy buttons. Faile

d calls open automatically. |

## Quick start

1. Open the workbench → the empty state creates **Chief** (team lead, automatic pinned chat).
2. Ask

Chief to build a team: *“Create a researcher and an engineer, then open a group with both.”*
3. Cha

t privately, or post a group discussion; mention members with `@Alice`.
4. Attach an image or a file

— the Bot gets the path and can read it.

## Architecture
[代码示例省略，未执行]
- **Host half** — plain ESM, `node:*` only; owns the ledger under `$DSH_HOME/dsh-bot/`, the session

runtime, the group dispatcher, the task engine, the avatar matcher and the model-facing tools.
- **C
lient half** — hand-written CommonJS bundled into `window.__ModuleLoader__.load` (no build toolchain

beyond a 60-line script); React elements only, host theme tokens.
- Every Bot reply is a real sessi
on turn; open it natively with one click.
